questions.question: In which of the following years did the revolt in the countryside of the Bombay Deccan occur?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1875**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **1875**__, the revolt in the countryside of the Bombay Deccan occurred.
 
• In the Bombay Deccan region, the British had introduced the Ryotwari settlement as the system of land revenue.
 
• Under this system, the revenue of land was fixed on a yearly basis.
 
• ​The revolt of the Bombay Deccan region
 
 
• The uprising began at Supa village in the district of Poona.
 
• In 1875, farmers attacked a marketplace where many moneylenders lived.
 
• They burnt account books and looted grain shops. They also torched the houses of people who were both traders and moneylenders.
 
• The farmers’ main motive was to destroy the account books of the moneylenders and they resorted to violence only when these books were not handed over to them.
 
• The movement also got support from the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha co-founded by M G Ranade.
 
• Accordingly, the Deccan Riots Commission was set up which presented a report to the British Parliament in 1878.
 
• In 1879, the Agriculturists Relief Act was passed which ensured that the farmers could not be arrested and imprisoned if they were unable to pay their debts.

questions.question: As of 26th January 2021, who is the Lok Sabha Speaker?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Om Birla**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As of 26th January 2021, **Om Birla**__ is the speaker of Lok Sabha since 19 June 2019.
 
• OM Birla was unanimously elected Speaker of the **17th Lok Sabha.**
 
• The Opposition did not field any candidate for the Speaker's post and the motion moved by PM Modi to choose the Kota-Bundi MP as Speaker was adopted by a voice vote.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• As per **Article 93 of the Indian Constitution**, the Lok Sabha has a Speaker and a Deputy Speaker.
 
• The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is the presiding officer of the Lok Sabha.
 
• The Speaker can be removed from office only on a resolution of the Lok Sabha passed by the absolute majority. It is also mandatory to give a minimum of 14 days' notice of the intention to move the resolution.
 
• The vote of the Speaker is called “Casting Vote” as it is cast in case of a tie in the number of votes.
 
• The first speaker of Lok Sabha was **Ganesh Vasudev Mavalankar.**
 
• The first female speaker of Lok Sabha is **Meira Kumar.**

• There are six fundamental rights enshrined in Part III (Articles 12 to 35) of the constitution of India.
 
• Fundamental rights apply universally to all citizens, irrespective of race, birthplace, religion, caste or gender.

questions.question: SHG promotes thrift in small proportion by a minimum contribution from each member of the group. What does 'H' stand for in SHG?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Help**__.

__
 
• **SHG**__- __**Self Help Group**__.
 
• Self Help Groups are groups of 10-20 people in a locality formed for any social or economic purpose.
 
• Self-help groups are seen as instruments for goals including empowering women, developing leadership abilities among the poor and the needy, increasing school enrolment and improving nutrition and the use of birth control.
 
• It can exist with or without registration.
 
• **NABARD developed the model of Self Help Group – Bank Linkage Programme **as a cost-effective mechanism for providing financial services to the unreached and underserved poor households.
 
• SHG perform the role of collective banks. They mobilize savings from the members and performs both debit and credit functions.
 
• Members may also make small regular savings contributions over a few months until there is enough money in the group to begin lending.

questions.question: Who among the following rulers is called the ‘Napoleon of India’?

__
 
• **Samudragupta **__is called the ‘Napoleon of India’.
 
• Samudragupta was the greatest ruler of the Gupta Dynasty and ruled till around 380 AD.
 
• The western scholars equate him with Napoleon and call him Indian Napoleon due to the extensive military conquests. 
 
• Some information about Samudragupta-
 
 
• He was the son of Chandragupta-I and Kumaradevi. He ascended the throne in 335 AD.
 
• Before his death, probably 4 or 5 years back, Chandragupta-I had publicly announced that Samudragupta would be his heir apparent and thus abdicated the throne in his favour.
 
• This was justified by the killer instincts of Samudragupta who displayed a greater degree of skill in the arts of both peace and war.
 
• But this nomination was perhaps not liked by many and coins of an obscure prince Kacha say that there was some trouble over the succession.
 
 
 
• Chandragupta I was a great ruler in the Gupta Empire and is generally considered as the originator of the Gupta line.
 
• **Ashoka** was the son of Bindusara. He promoted the spread of Buddhism across ancient Asia.

questions.question: What do you call the effect of splitting of a spectral line into several components in the presence of a static magnetic field?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zeeman effect**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Zeeman Effect**__

 __
 
• It is the name of the phenomena in physics and astronomy which involves the **splitting of a spectral line into two or more components of slightly different frequencies when the light source is placed in a magnetic field**.
 
• It is named after the Dutch physicist Pieter Zeeman.
 
• The effect is caused due to the distortion of the electron orbitals because of the magnetic field.
 
• This effect is very useful in investigating the charge/mass ratio and magnetic moment of an electron.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3960b9d2557a20b6a3f2c8a2a9c04c064ebafe04ec585bb3abd1d9311f3406d9.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Askaryan effect**

 
 
• It is the phenomenon whereby a particle travelling faster than the phase velocity of light in a dense dielectric medium (such as salt, ice) produces a shower of secondary charged particles.
 
• The Askaryan effect describes coherent electromagnetic radiation from high-energy cascades in dense media with a collective charge.
 
 
 
• **Bezold effect**
 
 
• It is an optical illusion.
 
• It is named after a German professor of meteorology, Wilhelm von Bezold.
 
• He discovered that a colour may appear different depending on its relation to adjacent colours.
 
• It happens when small areas of colour are interspersed.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2cde349b3d6197f7479ca03c197be9eb4ae9c5550bda653d74182c53cf2913f8.png] 

 
• **Domino effect**

 
 
• It is a cumulative effect produced when one event initiates a succession of similar events.
 
• It occurs when a significant change in the abundance (or presence) of one species results in a further change to the species composition or relative abundance of other species in a community.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/38a2c08dc788107a4fad01a3fb080d90b29e5abb6e7bf54b0ede0632ca9ffbe3.png]

questions.question: Deserts, rain forests, coral reefs and mangroves are features of _______ diversity.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ecological**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Deserts, rain forests, coral reefs and mangroves are features of **ecological**__ diversity.
 
• Ecological diversity is a type of biodiversity. It is at the ecosystem level.
 
• It is the** variation in the ecosystems **found in a region or the variation in ecosystems over the whole planet.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Cultural Diversity **is the existence of a variety of cultural groups within a society.
 
• **Species diversity **refers to the variety of species within a particular region. The richness of species in a given region provides a yardstick for species diversity. For example, the Western Ghats have a greater amphibian species diversity than the Eastern Ghats.
 
• **Genetic diversity **is the variation of genes within the species. This result distinct population of one, even the same species. It gives genetic variation within a population or varieties within one species.** **India has more than 50,000 genetically different strains of rice and 1,000 varieties of mango.

questions.question: As of 2020, which among the following is a permanent member of the United Nations Security Council?

• It was formed on 24 October 1945.
 
• Its powers consist of establishing peacekeeping operations, enacting international sanctions, and authorizing military action.
 
• The UNSC is the only UN body with the power to issue binding resolutions on member states. 
 
• It consists of 5 Permanent Members and 10 Non Permanent Members.
 
• **Permanent members are- China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom, and the United States**.

questions.question: Topaz is a _______ of fluorine and aluminium.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**silicate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Topaz is a **silicate**__ of fluorine and aluminium. 
 
• In other words, it is an aluminium silicate containing fluorine.
 
• It is the **hardest silicate mineral**.
 
• It is formed by fluorine-bearing vapours given off during the last stages of the crystallization of igneous rocks.
 
• It has a relatively low index of refraction.
 
• Common topaz in its natural state is colourless, though trace element impurities can make it pale blue, golden brown to yellow-orange.
 
• The most common use for topaz is as a gemstone in jewellery.
 
• The hardness also increases its tendency to break. Because of this, topaz is typically used for jewellery that will not be knocked around or come in contact with hard surfaces.

questions.question: In the periodic table, the highly electronegative halogens and the highly electropositive alkali metals are separated by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Noble gases__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Highly negative halogens require only one electron to complete their octet
 
• Noble gases are those whose octet is complicated.
 
• Alkali metal has only one extra electron in its outermost element they want to lose it to complete octet
 
• Hence, halogen and alkali metals are separated by noble gas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• In the periodic table of elements, there are seven horizontal rows of elements called periods. The vertical columns of elements are called groups, or families.
 
• The** Rare Earth Elements** make up the **middle block** of the periodic table.
 
• The **Rare Earth Elements** or transition metals occupy the short columns in the centre of the periodic table, between Group 2A and Group 3A. 
 
• They are sometimes called the *d*-block elements, since in this region the *d*-orbitals are being filled in, and are also referred to as B-group elements since in most numbering systems of the columns on the periodic table the numerals of these groups are followed by the letter B.

questions.question: Which of the following organs secretes hydrochloric acid that helps our body in killing pathogenic bacteria?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Stomach**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The stomach **__secretes hydrochloric acid that helps our body in killing pathogenic bacteria.
 
• Hydrochloric acid is the main component of gastric juice and is secreted by the parietal cells of the gastric mucosa in the fundus and corpus.
 
• It creates the ideal conditions for the protein-digesting enzymes to work.
 
• The potent hydrochloric acid kills bacteria, protecting your body from harmful microbes which can enter our body in food.
 
• Our stomach protects itself from being digested by its own enzymes, or burnt by the corrosive hydrochloric acid, by secreting sticky, neutralising mucus that clings to the stomach walls.
 
• If this layer becomes damaged in any way it can result in painful and unpleasant stomach ulcers.

questions.question: Which of the following state government launched the long-awaited policy of manufactured sand in January 2021?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The state government of** Rajasthan**__ launched the long-awaited policy of manufactured sand in January 2021.
 
• On 25th January 2021, Rajasthan Chief Minister Shri Ashok Gehlot released Rajasthan **M Sand Policy 2021**.
 
• **The policy aims to fulfil the demand for river sand for construction works across the state.**
 
• The M Sand policy will reduce dependency on the river sand and boost the use and production of M-Sand in Rajasthan.
 
• The policy gives industry status to the units producing it for construction work and reduces the dependence on bajri (riverbed sand).
 
• The Supreme Court had banned illegal mining on riverbeds in 2017.
 
• The policy would help create employment opportunities through new units and resolve the issue of huge quantities of waste generated in the mining areas.
 
• The policy will enable the investors to set up M-sand units by utilising the incentives and facilities offered by the State government.
 
• It will also help in environmental protection and generate faith among the public in the efficacy of M-sand for construction works.
